report:
The claim is **true**, not false: Kyleena (levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system, 19.5 mg) is FDA-approved for prevention of pregnancy for up to 5 years.

This is confirmed directly by the official FDA label itself, which states: "Kyleena is indicated to prevent pregnancy for up to 5 years" (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/208224s000lbl.pdf). The DailyMed record of Kyleena's current prescribing information—sourced from the FDA-approved structured product label—repeats this verbatim: "Kyleena is a progestin-containing intrauterine system (IUS) indicated for prevention of pregnancy for up to 5 years" (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080).

Bayer's own product monograph corroborates this, noting that "Following insertion into the uterine cavity, KYLEENA... is effective for up to 5 years. KYLEENA must be removed by the end of the fifth year" (https://www.bayer.com/sites/default/files/2020-11/kyleena-pm-en.pdf). This is consistent with the FDA approval history documented by Drugs.com, which notes the approval was based on Phase III trial data showing a Pearl Index of 0.29 through five years, with the device found "more than 99 percent effective for each year of use in preventing pregnancy" (https://www.drugs.com/history/kyleena.html).

All four primary and authoritative sources—FDA's official label, DailyMed's regulatory database entry, Bayer's product monograph, and clinical trial-based approval history—agree unanimously that Kyleena is approved and clinically validated for pregnancy prevention for up to five years. There is no conflicting or contradictory evidence among the retrieved sources. The claim as stated is accurate, and the premise that it is false is not supported by any available evidence.
